content.title: Material Guide | Spatial Growth Resolves into a Flat Layout
content.summary: Starting from a tiny material anchor point, let the same continuous material first guide the movement of the camera, then form a thick and readable structure and expand it into the environment. Finally, by looking down and increasing the dimension, the three-dimensional scene is compressed into a flat layout that maintains the relationship between characters and materials.

quick_start.input_format: Stable subject + tiny material origin + same material to guide mirror movement/form solid structure/expand into environment + single elevation + retain historical layout final state
quick_start.recommended_input: In the polar archives, a brass survey beetle pulls a single frost filament from an ice seed; the frost filament guides the camera, forms the physical K-42 code, and unfolds the crystalline chart chamber, only to be raised once, condensing the beetle, code, and path into a readable field chart page.
required_anchors: Introduce one small material guide on the same optical axis as a stable subject.
Keep one continuous material family responsible for camera guidance, color accumulation and spatial growth.
Expand the same material into an environment that still contains the original subject and prior palette.
Use one late camera rise to resolve the dimensional scene into a held graphic sheet that preserves subject and material history.
usage_steps: Replace the example subject, setting, and surface details with an original concept.
Keep every required anchor and Creative DNA invariant causally visible.
Choose the MiniMax H3 or Seedance 2.0 prompt and fill only the declared variable slots.
Check duration, event order, camera continuity, sound, and anti-copy constraints before generation.
applicable_scope: Starting from a tiny material anchor point, let the same continuous material first guide the movement of the camera, then form a thick and readable structure and expand it into the environment. Finally, by looking down and increasing the dimension, the three-dimensional scene is compressed into a flat layout that maintains the relationship between characters and materials.
Original 4–15 second concepts that can preserve every required anchor.
MiniMax H3 or Seedance 2.0 projects that need a reusable causal video structure.
not_suitable_for: Requests that copy the source identity, setting, props, dialogue, or shot order.
Concepts that cannot show all required anchors inside the target duration.
Long-form exposition or unrelated multi-location stories without a compact causal chain.

creative_dna.mechanism: Begin with one small material guide aligned to a stable subject. Keep that same material visually continuous as it pulls the camera, accumulates color and depth, becomes one readable physical structure, and expands into an inhabitable environment. Reserve one final camera rise that compresses the dimensional world into a held graphic sheet while preserving the subject and material history.

invariants.rule: Introduce one small material guide on the same optical axis as a stable subject.
invariants.purpose: Creates a precise origin for the transformation.
invariants.ablation_failure: Without a small origin and stable subject, the sequence starts as an ungrounded effects montage.

invariants.rule: Keep one continuous material family responsible for camera guidance, color accumulation and spatial growth.
invariants.purpose: Makes every phase feel causally related.
invariants.ablation_failure: Changing material rules between phases breaks the transformation chain.

invariants.rule: Let the material form one readable, depth-bearing structure inside the scene and hold it briefly.
invariants.purpose: Provides a recognition checkpoint before scale expansion.
invariants.ablation_failure: Flat overlay copy or unreadable decoration cannot prove physical integration.

invariants.rule: Expand the same material into an environment that still contains the original subject and prior palette.
invariants.purpose: Turns a local effect into a world-scale payoff without losing identity.
invariants.ablation_failure: A disconnected new room would read as a scene swap.

invariants.rule: Use one late camera rise to resolve the dimensional scene into a held graphic sheet that preserves subject and material history.
invariants.purpose: Closes spatial spectacle with an inspectable format change.
invariants.ablation_failure: An arbitrary end card would not prove continuity with the preceding world.

slots.name: lead_subject
slots.constraint: An original stable subject or pair with a readable role.

slots.name: setting
slots.constraint: A new setting with fixed spatial anchors and no source-specific surface.

slots.name: escalation_variable
slots.constraint: One causal variable that changes through visible stages.

slots.name: performance_rule
slots.constraint: A restrained acting or motion rule that keeps the mechanism legible.

slots.name: camera_grammar
slots.constraint: An information order that proves each state without copying source shot boundaries.

slots.name: payoff
slots.constraint: A clean final physical, informational or social consequence.

slots.name: sound_family
slots.constraint: An original hierarchy of diegetic cues; no unsupported source-audio claim.

anti_copy_exclusions: the source black-haired fashion model and printed white dress
the source watercolor ribbon palette and ivory paper gallery
the source flower-petal chamber and fashion-ad poster layout

instantiations.concept: In an original polar research archive, one autonomous brass survey beetle releases a hair-thin frost filament. The filament guides a low camera, grows into the readable physical code K-42, opens into a crystalline wind-map chamber, then one final overhead rise resolves beetle, code and ice paths into a held field-chart sheet.
